speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a newborn presenting with respiratory distress. To understand your condition, can you tell me how many days old you are and when the symptoms started?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born at 33 weeks of gestation. The newborn is presenting with respiratory distress 2 hours after birth. The mother had an uneventful pregnancy until premature onset of labor. There was no significant prenatal care history mentioned.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS).

Given your history of being born at 33 weeks gestation with respiratory distress starting immediately after birth, the lack of prenatal care and premature labor strongly suggest immature lung surfactant production. I will proceed to confirm this with a diagnostic test.

REQUEST TEST: Arterial_Blood_Gas (ABG) to check for hypoxemia and respiratory acidosis.
REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_X-Ray to look for the classic "ground-glass" appearance and air bronchograms associated with RDS.
